metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Little Meadows, PA
metaDescription: Little Meadows sits in Susquehanna County near the New York line — one of Pennsylvania's most actively drilled dry-gas counties. What that means for you.
heroLead: Little Meadows sits near the New York border in Susquehanna County, one of the most consistently active dry-gas Marcellus counties anywhere in Pennsylvania.
intro: Small acreage adds up fast in Susquehanna County when operators are laying out drilling units, and Little Meadows-area landowners have watched that happen firsthand for over a decade. A single unit can pull together dozens of individual family tracts, each contributing a small share, which is part of why this county has such a dense record of leases and royalty history compared to many other parts of the state.

sections.heading: Why Small Tracts Still Matter in an Active Unit
paragraphs: Even a modest acreage near Little Meadows can carry real value if it sits inside a producing or permitted unit, because your royalty share is based on your proportion of the unit's total acreage, not on your tract standing alone. We check unit participation directly rather than assuming a small parcel doesn't count.

Because Little Meadows sits so close to the state line, some families here also own smaller parcels just across in New York, which makes for an interesting contrast once they see how differently the two states have handled gas development.

sections.heading: Susquehanna's Sustained Development
paragraphs: Coterra and its predecessor Cabot Oil & Gas have run long-term development programs across Susquehanna County, and that consistency means Little Meadows-area parcels usually have real, current production data behind them rather than speculative projections.

sections.heading: What We Confirm Before Any Number
paragraphs: We pull your deed, check whether a unit already includes your parcel, and look at nearby royalty history before building a range. If your acreage is unleased and open, that changes the picture from a parcel already committed to fixed lease terms.

faqs.question: Is my small acreage worth checking if it's near a big producing unit?
faqs.answer: Yes — unit participation is proportional, so even modest acreage inside an active Susquehanna County unit can carry meaningful value.

faqs.question: How active is drilling around Little Meadows specifically?
faqs.answer: Susquehanna County overall has been one of the most consistently drilled dry-gas counties in the state; we check the specific status for your parcel directly.

faqs.question: What if my land isn't in a unit yet?
faqs.answer: Unleased, unassigned acreage is evaluated differently than a producing interest, generally with more uncertainty but sometimes more upside — we'll walk through both.

faqs.question: How is a small interest actually paid out if it's part of a big unit?
faqs.answer: Royalty is calculated as your acreage's percentage of the total unit acreage, applied to the unit's total production, so even a modest Little Meadows tract earns its proportional share.
